# nuzur

This codebase is generated by [nuzur](https://nuzur.com) `go-code-gen` from the project's
schema (entities, enums, relationships, indexes). It is regenerated on every schema
change or configuration change.

---

## ⚠️ Rules for AI Assistants & LLMs

1. **Generated files are off limits.** Every generated file carries the marker
   `Code generated by nuzur go-code-gen. DO NOT EDIT.` near the top (as a `//`, `#`,
   `--` or `<!-- -->` comment, depending on the file type), and every generated file is
   listed in `.nuzur-codegen-manifest.json` at the project root. Check for the marker
   before editing anything.
2. **Edits to generated files are lost.** The next generation run overwrites them, and
   files that are no longer produced are deleted using the manifest. If the user asks
   for a change to a generated file anyway, tell them it will be overwritten before you
   make it.
3. **Files without the marker are yours (and the user's) to edit.** They are never
   overwritten and never deleted by the generator.
4. **Schema changes belong in nuzur, not in Go.** To add an entity, field, enum, index
   or relationship, change the project schema in nuzur and regenerate. Do not hand-edit
   entity structs, the SQL schema/queries, or the protobuf definitions to add them —
   those edits will not survive and will not reach the database.
5. **The custom application zone is disabled for this project.** There is no user-owned
   directory for custom endpoints. It can be turned on in the nuzur go-code-gen
   extension configuration (`custom_enabled`, with an optional `custom_dir`, default
   `app`); regeneration will then scaffold it once.

## Codebase Structure

* **`core/entity/`**: Go structs for the data models, plus `types/` and
  `mapper/` helpers. Fully regenerated on every run.
* **`enums/`**: Go constants and helpers for the schema's enums.
* **`idl/`**: Protocol Buffer definitions and the generated gRPC stubs
  (`idl/gen`), plus the gRPC server in `idl/server`.
* **`core/`**: The business-logic layer.
  * **`core/repository/`**: Database access generated via `sqlc`
    (`sql/schema`, `sql/queries` and the generated `gen/` code).
  * **`core/module/<entity>/`**: CRUD per entity — fetch by index, list with
    pagination, insert/update/upsert, delete.
* **`auth/`**: Keycloak (OIDC) middleware.
* **`info/`**: Self-documenting "what's deployed" HTML page served at the HTTP root `/`.
* **`config/`**: Configuration loading plus `base.yaml` / `cli.yaml`. **Regenerated in
  full on every run** — never keep secrets or hand-edits here; supply real values at
  deploy time (or via the `CONFIG` / `ENV` environment variables).
* **`main.go`**: Entrypoint; wires every enabled component with Uber Fx.
* **`.nuzur-codegen-manifest.json`**: Inventory of every generated file. Used to clean
  up files that are no longer generated; user-added files are never listed.

---

## Runtime Surface

* **gRPC** on port `6005` — health and reflection registered.
* **HTTP** on port `8085`.
* Keycloak (OIDC): send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the middleware validates it.
* `GET /` — the info page describing this deployment.

## Deploying

If this app has been deployed at least once, **`.nuzur/last-deploy.json`** records
exactly how: provider, server, hostnames, image repository, project version and
database connection. Repeat that deploy with

```
nuzur-cli deploy --deploy-config .nuzur/last-deploy.json
```

Read that file before asking the user how the app is deployed — it is the answer,
and it is the only place the answer lives in this repository.

Three things to know about it:

* **It is generated.** The CLI rewrites it after every successful deploy, so do not
  hand-edit it. Unlike the rest of the generated tree it carries no `DO NOT EDIT`
  marker (it is not produced by `go-code-gen`), but the same rule applies. Keep a
  separate file if you want a deploy spec you maintain, and pass it explicitly.
* **It carries no credentials.** The database password, the SSH key path and the
  local workspace path are deliberately excluded, which is what makes it safe to
  commit. The database is named by a connection uuid that resolves server-side.
* **It works from a fresh clone.** The workspace is recovered from the file's own
  location, so the command above runs on a machine that has never deployed this
  app.

If the file is absent, this app has either never been deployed or was last deployed
by a CLI too old to write one. Ask the user for the deploy command rather than
guessing at one — a deploy that resolves fewer hostnames than the release serves
will take a live front door offline.
